title: Agentic AI Frameworks: Architectures, Protocols, and Design Challenges
authors: Hana Derouiche, Zaki Brahmi, Haithem Mazeni
preview: Systematic review and comparative analysis of leading agentic AI frameworks including CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, and MetaGPT, covering architectures, protocols, and design challenges.
summary: Provides a structured taxonomy of agentic AI frameworks, evaluating architectural principles, communication mechanisms, memory management, and safety guardrails across seven major frameworks. Conducts an in-depth analysis of inter-agent communication protocols including Contract Net Protocol, Agent-to-Agent (A2A), Agent Network Protocol (ANP), and Agora. Identifies key limitations and open challenges in scalability, robustness, and interoperability for autonomous AI systems.
datacenter: Relevant to AI-on-iA infrastructure planning: the framework comparison and protocol analysis directly informs how head-node orchestration layers should be designed for multi-agent agentic workloads at datacenter scale, including considerations for fault isolation and communication overhead.
metrics: Key result signal: comparative architectural taxonomy across seven agentic frameworks with identified gaps in scalability, safety guardrails, and cross-framework interoperability.
